query: For high-entropy nanoalloys in high-temperature applications, what governs structural and chemical stability, and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, propose a controlled comparison that would distinguish it from alternatives, predict observations relative to a baseline, define the boundaries of the prediction, identify supporting evidence from the background, and state a falsifying outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In fcc high-entropy nanoalloy (HENA) particles (5–20 nm), high-temperature structural and chemical stability is governed primarily by surface-energy–driven radial segregation moderated by pairwise mixing enthalpies: elements with lower surface energy enrich the surface to minimize γ, and whether this stabilizes or destabilizes the nanoalloy depends on the sign of the mixing enthalpy among the surface-enriched species. Specifically, for equimolar CoCrFeNiX, X = Cu (low surface energy, positive mixing enthalpy with Fe/Co/Cr) forms a Cu-rich shell that accelerates surface diffusion, de-mixing, and coarsening, whereas X = Pt (high surface energy, predominantly negative mixing enthalpy with Ni/Co) suppresses deleterious surface segregation and maintains chemical homogeneity, yielding slower coarsening under identical high-temperature exposure.
generation.material_initial_state: Two sets of equimolar, single-phase fcc nanoparticles: CoCrFeNiCu and CoCrFeNiPt, each 10 ± 2 nm diameter, initially near-homogeneous composition (±2 at% element-to-element variation by atom probe tomography), minimal initial short-range order, dispersed on inert supports to avoid direct particle-particle necking.
generation.intervention: Isothermal annealing at 0.65 Tm (relative to each alloy’s measured solidus) for 10–20 hours in high-purity Ar (≤1 ppm O2/H2O) with identical thermal history for both compositions; no reactive gases; same particle areal density to equalize sintering probability.
generation.conditions: Inert atmosphere (Ar), low oxygen and moisture, heating/cooling rates 5 K/min, steady temperature 0.65 Tm for 15 h; particles immobilized on an amorphous carbon or MgO support prepassivated to minimize metal–support reactions; characterization at room temperature immediately after anneal.
generation.structural_mediator: A radius-dependent, radially graded composition (core–shell) formed by Gibbsian surface segregation: a shell enriched in the lowest-γ element (Cu in CoCrFeNiCu; Ni or Co for CoCrFeNiPt) with a complementary core enriched in higher-γ elements, and the associated short-range order within the core.
generation.mechanism: Surface-energy minimization drives enrichment of low-γ elements at the nanoparticle surface. The thermodynamic driving force for segregation scales with Δγ_surf among constituent elements and surface-to-volume ratio. Whether this segregation stabilizes or destabilizes the nanoalloy depends on the pairwise mixing enthalpy among the surface-enriched species: positive H_mix among surface-enriched neighbors (e.g., Cu with Fe/Co/Cr) promotes chemical de-mixing and fast surface diffusion pathways, accelerating coarsening and phase separation; negative or near-zero H_mix (e.g., Pt with Ni/Co, and Pt’s reluctance to occupy the surface due to high γ) sustains a more homogeneous lattice and suppresses surface-mediated transport, slowing coarsening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the Pt-containing baseline, CoCrFeNiCu nanoparticles will (i) exhibit stronger surface enrichment of the low-γ element (Cu) manifested as a larger positive radial composition gradient (significant Cu excess in the outer ~1 nm), (ii) show earlier onset of chemical de-mixing (detectable secondary peaks or SRO changes), and (iii) coarsen faster under identical conditions (larger increase in mean particle diameter and broader size distribution). The Pt-containing nanoparticles will retain closer-to-bulk stoichiometry at the surface, maintain more uniform short-range order, and display a lower coarsening rate. The expected direction of differences is robust; the exact magnitudes (e.g., fold-change in coarsening rate, absolute surface excess) are uncertain without calibration.
generation.baseline: Equimolar CoCrFeNiPt nanoparticles processed and annealed identically, serving as a matched-composition baseline with reduced tendency for deleterious surface segregation compared to CoCrFeNiCu.
generation.boundary: Applies to single-phase fcc equimolar HENA nanoparticles with diameters ~5–20 nm; inert (non-oxidizing, non-sulfidizing) atmospheres; temperatures in the range 0.55–0.7 Tm where bulk melting and long-range ordering transformations are absent; minimal particle–particle necking; supports that do not significantly alter surface energies or induce strong metal–support interactions. Predictions may not hold for larger particles (>50 nm), bcc or multiphase HEAs, oxidizing environments, or compositions with strong ordered intermetallic propensities at the test temperature.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative magnitude of surface enrichment, the exact coarsening rate ratio, and the temperature at which segregation saturates are uncertain and may depend on synthesis-induced defects, initial short-range order, and support interactions. Unexpected oxide formation or particle necking could dominate kinetics and obscure surface-energy–driven effects. Pt’s specific interactions may vary with actual VEC and local chemistry; alternative high-γ substitutions could be tested to generalize.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize matched CoCrFeNiCu and CoCrFeNiPt nanoparticles (10 ± 2 nm), confirm initial single-phase fcc and near-homogeneous composition by XRD and APT. Deposit on identical inert supports at low coverage. Anneal both sets side-by-side at 0.65 Tm for 15 h in high-purity Ar. Characterize: (1) radial composition profiles by angle-resolved XPS and/or APT with 3D reconstructions; (2) particle size distributions before/after anneal by TEM; (3) short-range order evolution by synchrotron total scattering/PDF or diffuse scattering.
measurements: Surface vs bulk composition (at% per element) with depth resolution ~0.5–1 nm
Mean particle diameter and geometric standard deviation before and after anneal
Time-resolved coarsening kinetics (mean diameter vs time) from in situ TEM or sequential ex situ anneals
Indicators of chemical de-mixing (secondary phases in PDF/XRD; changes in Warren–Cowley SRO parameters)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Falsify the hypothesis if, under identical conditions, CoCrFeNiCu does not exhibit greater low-γ element surface enrichment than CoCrFeNiPt (i.e., no statistically significant increase in Cu surface excess relative to Pt-containing sample at 95% confidence) and does not show a higher coarsening rate (no statistically significant increase in d̄ growth rate or final mean size), or if CoCrFeNiPt exhibits equal or greater surface segregation-driven de-mixing and faster coarsening than CoCrFeNiCu.
